newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom, Havas in final stages of ODA talks.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom, Havas in final stages of ODA talks.

text.p: Negotiations over France Telecom buying back Office d'Annonces (ODA) from media group Havas are in their final phase, Gerard Eymery, chairman of France Telecom Multimedia, told a news conference.

ODA, created as a 50-50 joint venture by France Telecom and Havas, became a unit of Havas in 1994 when France Telecom exchanged its ODA holding for 4.3 percent of Havas. ODA handles all advertising carried in France Telecom's telephone directories.
Havas said on February 21 that the two groups could accord each other buy and sell options for ODA exercisable between January 1, 2000 and 21 December, 2003.
Asked if the buy-back of ODA could be the occasion for France Telecom to pull out of Havas's capital entirely, Eymery said he had no information.
"That is a question which relates to general discussions. On that I have no information. I do not think the two things are linked," he said.
France Telecom had said it wanted to clarify the position of ODA earlier this month when Generale des Eaux increased its share in Havas.

Generale des Eaux already competes with France Telecom in mobile telephones. It has set up a telecommunications subsidiary, Cegetel, which aims to be the main competitor of France Telecom across the board after liberalisation of European telecommunications markets in 1998.
As part of that liberalisation France Telecom is to be partially privatised, with a first tranche of the sell-off expected in May.
A source close to the talks said France Telecom did not want Cegetel to have access to ODA.
In 1995 ODA made a net profit of 123.7 million francs on turnover of 4.05 billion francs. Figures for 1996 are not yet available. WEM/SLA
